scientific_hypothesis: A two-tier perturbation scheme with ±3% noise on layers 1-12 and ±12% independent perturbation on layers 13-22 will produce higher target scores than uniform perturbation by decoupling fine-scale phase matching from spectral envelope shaping.
expected_advantages: Two-tier perturbation may escape local optima that uniform perturbation cannot
Decoupling phase and envelope tuning could better separate the two narrow passbands
Maintains same material pair and layer count as prior iterations for fair comparison
Builds on iteration_08 baseline which achieved 0.698 target score
known_risks: ZnS and MgF2 refractive indices in 4-5 μm range are recalled approximations; actual dispersion data from registry will determine true performance
Daimon-20 substrate index at these wavelengths is recalled as ~1.42 but registry data is authoritative
The 478.0/815.0 nm baseline comes from iteration_08 candidate 1, not from independent quarter-wave calculation at band centers
±3% and ±12% perturbation bounds are heuristic choices; optimal ranges are unknown without literature
22 layers may be insufficient for sharp dual-band separation; 24 layers might perform better but this route fixes 22 for consistency
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase relative to iteration_08's 0.6986 if the two-tier scheme finds better local optima
valid_candidates count should remain similar to prior iterations (around 9) if perturbation bounds are physically reasonable
tightest_margin should not decrease significantly across rounds if the design remains manufacturable
thicknesses_nm for layers 1-12 should cluster near 478.0/815.0 nm baseline with small deviations
thicknesses_nm for layers 13-22 should show wider distribution reflecting the larger perturbation allowance
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if valid_candidates falls below 3 for two consecutive rounds, reduce perturbation bounds by half and continue
if tightest_margin becomes negative for all candidates, relax the ±12% bound on layers 13-22 to ±8% and continue
